thread.title: PTC's Opportunity In The IoT Market - PTC Inc. (NASDAQ:PTC)

author: Jorge Acrisio
title: PTC's Opportunity In The IoT Market - PTC Inc. (NASDAQ:PTC)
text:
Since acquiring the Kepware and Vuforia businesses back in 2016, PTC Inc. (NASDAQ: PTC ) has been able to expand its portfolio of product and service lifecycle management (PLM and SLM) by integrating these Internet of Things (IoT) solutions into its business. The company is trying to gain its own market share in the manufacturing IoT space from more well-known competitors such as SAP (NYSE: SAP ), Cisco (NASDAQ: CSCO ), and Oracle (NYSE: ORCL ), as these companies continue diversifying their services while striving to succeed in this flourishing market.
The high-growth opportunity that the industrial IoT market offers PTC has caused investors and analysts to see the company in a different, more optimistic way. The firm's ability to cross-sell IoT solutions to its existing customers could result in significant revenue growth for the next 5 years, while the company continues to strengthen its early leadership position in this market.
Despite the fact that 88% of managers and executives do not fully understand the underlying business models and long-term implications of industrial IoT applications in their operations, PTC can make its way through this market thanks to its strong relationship with its customers. Most of these customers have built their manufacturing processes around PTC’s software, and the company can easily insert new IoT solutions into their manufacturing ecosystems.
In addition, the company's relationship with its customers has also changed in recent years. PTC has been in the process of transitioning from selling perpetual licenses to a subscription-based model in an effort to generate sustainable growth in the long term.
Source: Image extracted from the second quarterly report of 2018.
Overall, the company has been presenting a new investment thesis during the past two years, which is based on the prospect of the IoT industry and its plans to generate sustainable growth through recurring revenues.
PTC’s shift in revenue and the IoT adoption Although the company suffered from a short-term decrease in revenue, which was caused by the decrease in sales of perpetual licenses while it was transitioning to a subscription-based model, in the recent quarter, executives are beginning to report revenue growth as this new strategy starts to deliver tangible value for the company.
Source: Data extracted from filing from the SEC.
The company's ThingWorx platform is responsible for the majority of its growth, as large companies have shown a great demand for it during the last two quarters. In the first half of 2018, companies like Exxon Mobil (NYSE: XOM ), Airbus ( OTCPK:EADSY ), and the Chinese airframe company AVEC, are using this technology to build, deploy and integrate applications in their manufacturing processes. Moreover, the company has recently made expansion deals with numerous companies in the Americas and Europe, serving different industries such as airlines, automotive, financial, food and beverage, and technology.
In addition to these deals, the company has started strategic partnerships with leaders in the IoT and augmented reality (AR) industries. The most recent partnerships align the company’s ThingWorx platform with Apple's (NASDAQ: AAPL ) ARKit platform , Google's (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) ARCore software, and Microsoft’s (NASDAQ: MSFT ) Azure IoT suite. These partnerships further consolidate the company’s IoT technology as they become consistently recognized as market leading solutions.
On the other hand, while IoT products still represent a minor proportion of total revenues, this technology is in fact the fastest growing for the third year in a row. In the second quarter of 2018, IoT products reported a 33% increase from the same period of the previous year, as well as a strong bookings growth between 30% and 40%, which further confirms that the majority of PTC's customers are adopting this new technology. IoT revenue continues to come from a wide variety of vertical markets and use cases, but led by the industrial factory operations.
To summarize, over the past two years the company has been building a robust ecosystem that allows manufacturers to plan, design, validate, produce, operate, and service products. As a result, the business model offers higher switching costs for its customers since it now covers a broader spectrum of their manufacturing processes. These switching costs further help to strengthen the new subscription model as more and more clients are converting to these contracts.
Source: Image extracted from the second quarterly report of 2018.
However, despite the fact that the IoT solutions are being widely accepted by customers, the company still holds less market share than its main competitors. Given that the industrial IoT applications promise to be a game-changing trend in many industries, large service providers are diversifying their offerings and developing their own platforms as they try to gain market share in this growing industry.
PTC competes with larger providers of industrial IoT platforms that are more well-known and hold a greater market share; the most significant among them are SAP’s Leonardo IoT Bridge, Cisco’s Kinetic platform, and, and Oracle’s IoT cloud service. These companies are more capitalized and have more resources, representing a competitive risk that could intensify in the future.
Moreover, in recent years, an increasing amount of new companies funded through venture capital that are developing their own IoT applications has been observed. Given the early stage of the industry, large technological companies can make their way into this market through M&A as they pursue the same growth prospects of the IoT market.
Overall, while the subscription model allows PTC to leverage on the recurring revenues from its clients, and ensures sustained growth and profitability in its lines of businesses, it seems that the company’s long-term growth is highly dependent on the success of their IoT solutions. In the meantime, PTC has established an early leadership position in the industrial IoT market through its acquisitions, partnership with leading developers, and relationship with its customers.
Valuations The stock price seems to be in a strong uptrend despite short term market corrections and periods of market instability, maintaining this secular trend for more than 2 years. The shift of the stock price from being practically stagnant in 2016 to increasing by more than 200% since then is mostly associated with the company’s consolidation in the industrial IoT.
Following the acquisition of the Vuforia business from Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM ) at the end of 2015, and the IoT software development company Kepware at the beginning of 2016, a new wave of investors jumped in, attracted by the prospects of the industrial IoT market and the improvements that these new acquisitions have brought the company. Given the recent nature of the IoT industry, there are few players that are gaining their own market share with little competitions, which allows them to trade at a considerable premium.
Nevertheless, maintaining high valuations always comes with the risk of a sudden correction. Despite the improvements in sales and the consolidation in the IoT market, the company holds high levels of uncertainty that can translate to sell-off if the market conditions suddenly change.

Looking forward, the subscription model is expected to deliver more growth in the middle term as the company puts an end to the sale of perpetual licenses. The new business mix seems to be more profitable, and is leading to a margin expansion that can increase even more when the company improves its marketing costs and becomes more efficient, leveraging on its recurring revenues.
In addition to the subscription model, the acquisitions of the IoT businesses are expected to deliver significant revenue growth in the long term, reporting double-digit growth per year. These estimates are based on the early customer adoption, and the forecasted outlook of the IoT market.
PTC PS Ratio (TTM) data by YCharts
Summarizing, while the company can expect to report near-term growth and reductions in its cost structure as it continues moving toward its subscription model, there is no doubt that the IoT space represents the most important growth opportunity for the company in the long term. Nevertheless, until the company begins to earn a significant part of its income from this new revenue stream, valuations will remain sustained by expectations rather than the current results.
